Hi Jane —

Great to connect — thanks for the concise summary. Recap & immediate next steps from our side below.

Recap / status:
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (Security) certified (report available under NDA).
- Data roles: Redwood acts as a Processor for customer-provided data; customers (like Acme) are Controllers.
- Processing details: We process input data to produce model outputs and do not use customer data to train models unless explicitly agreed. We support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.

Attachments included:
- Acme_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (Redwood standard DPA — please review; redlines expected)
- SCC_Module_Comparison.xlsx (short comparison of the EU SCC modules and our recommended options)

Recommendation on SCC module:
- For your use case (Acme as Controller, Redwood as Processor) we typically use the controller-to-processor module (Module 2 under the EU SCC framework). That module covers the Controller -> Processor relationship and is the right fit unless your legal team requests a different third-party mapping.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please review the attached DPA and SCC sheet.
2) Confirm whether Acme will sign Redwood's DPA and which SCC module you prefer (we recommend Module 2).
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call between Acme legal/risk and our legal/security team to walk through any redlines.
4) We'll start the vendor security questionnaire on our side and return a partially completed version for your review (leads: Rishi + Neha).

If you want, propose times for the legal/risk call next week and we'll send a calendar invite.
